description: There are significant differences in response to psychiatric illness across cultures. Delves into the neuroscience underlying mood disorder, investigating current pharmacological treatments and sociocultural influences on treatment outcomes.
restriction: No School of Biological Sciences students

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Origin of Life
description: Biochemical explanations for the origin of life are presented. Topics include definitions of life, the first replicating molecules, the first catalyzed biosynthesis and metabolism, the origin of cells (compartmentalization) and the origins of information and the genetic code.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Media on the Mind
description: Surveys an ever-increasing collection of research, suggesting modern technology and social media are changing in the way our brains function.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Stem Cells and Brain Repair
description: Students introduced to the field of regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders examined. Discussion of opportunities, challenges, and implications of this research.

description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

description: Students carry out two activities: (1) leading discussions about HIV/AIDS (predominantly regarding sociological and personal reactions) among students taking the AIDS Fundamentals course and (2) literature research about biomedical aspects of AIDS.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

description: Investigates stress at a psychological, physiological, and molecular level, and provides a current overview of the field of stress research.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: The Mind-Body Connection in the Neuroscience of Well-Being
description: Explores research that provides insight into how exercise, diet, sleep, contemplative practices such as mindfulness and meditation, and contemporary psychological therapeutic approaches alter brain function in beneficial ways to promote positive mental health well-being.

Discusses tropical biomes, their population, community, ecosystem processes, and possible means of conservation of biodiversity.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biodiversity & Conservation
description: A biological perspective on the current environmental crisis. The origin, evolution, and value of biological diversity. Extinction and depletion caused by overexploitation, habitat loss, and pollution. Conservation through habitat preservation and restoration, captive breeding, cryopreservation.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Vaccines
description: Focus on introducing vaccines, covering how vaccines work, as well as how they are tested. Introduction to the immune system, to facilitate understanding how vaccines function. Also covers types of vaccines, clinical trials, and vaccine hesitancy.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Human Development
description: Processes leading to the birth of a healthy child and the avoidance of birth defects. Male and female reproductive systems, hormonal control of egg-sperm formations, sexual intercourse, contraception, venereal diseases, fertilization, cell division, embryonic development, fetal physiology.
restriction: No School of Biological Sciences students

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution and the Modern World
description: Pandemics, disease, antibiotic resistance, your pets, the food you eat: evolution has shaped our world. Discusses the intellectual development of evolution and illustrates, with current events, that evolution is happening all around us, all the time.
restriction: No School of Biological Sciences students

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Biology Research
description: Students use the scientific method, ask and answer questions about environmental DNA, and develop professional skills applicable to any major or career. Focuses on the development of quantitative reasoning, science inquiry, and collaboration skills. Materials Fee
restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Curriculum
description: Initiation, planning, and coordination of student-run courses.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: From DNA to Organisms
description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology of organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).
restriction: Nursing Science majors, Pharmaceutical Sciences majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Unaffiliated majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. BIO SCI 93 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: From Organisms to Ecosystems
description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93
restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Unaffiliated majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. BIO SCI 1A may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 94

title: Organisms to Ecosystems - Introduction to Biology Research Analysis
description: Helps students learn how to use the scientific method, ask and answer questions about environmental DNA, and develop professional skills. Students learn how to design and conduct experiments, analyze data, interpret graphs, and communicate their findings. Materials fee.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Genetics
description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.

title: Biochemistry
description: Structure and properties of proteins; major biochemical pathways and mechanisms for their control.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97) and (CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2C with a minimum grade of C-)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Molecular Biology
description: Biochemistry and replication of nucleic acids; molecular genetics; protein biosynthesis; genetic code; regulation of expression of genetic information; biochemical evolution.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Nutrition Science
description: An introduction to nutrition science, integrating concepts from biology, biochemistry, microbiology, physiology, and psychology to explain the interaction between nutrients and the human body. Biological basis of nutrient standards is analyzed. Effects of nutrition, behavior, exercises on health/disease.

instructors.department: Cath Lab - UCI Health Los Alamitos

instructors.name: Nisa K Zacharias
instructors.title: HS Assistant Clinical Professor
instructors.department: Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Science of Cooking
description: The kitchen is used as a laboratory to introduce fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and physics. A molecular/cellular analysis of cooking, including concepts such as protein structure, browning reactions, colloids, emulsions, carbohydrate metabolism, and development of flavor/texture through biochemical transformations.
restriction: No School of Biological Sciences students

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biotech Basics
description: An overview of current biotechnology. Discusses the biological/molecular basis of novel therapies for diseases, modification of human genes, human genome project, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, and genetically modified food. Targeted for students interested in modern breakthroughs in biology.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Diseases of the Twenty-First Century
description: Why do we get sick? An introduction to the biological basis of human disease, including diseases of the cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, and reproductive systems. Case studies present diagnosis, treatment, and prevention protocols. Inheritable and infectious diseases also discussed.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Horticulture Science
description: Scientific principles of horticulture at the UCI Arboretum. Taxonomy, plant life history strategies; experiments with seed dormancy; morphological adaptations for specialized sexual and clonal reproduction; basics of plant propagation and ecological restoration.  Materials fee.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Physiology of Fitness
description: An introduction to the organ systems of the human body, including muscle, cardiovascular, immune, and reproductive systems, with an emphasis on how the body responds to exercise, diet, and disease.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biology of Oriental Medicine
description: With lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on learning, the theory and practice of herbal medicine, acupuncture, qigong, and manipulative therapies are explained in Western biomedical terms. The latest basic and clinical research advances in each area are also described.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Global Change Biology
description: Field trips and lectures that address ways in which humans are altering the global environment, with consequences for the ecology of animals, plants, and microbes.
restriction: No School of Biological Sciences students

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Complementary and Alternative Medicine
description: Basic and clinical research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., herbal medicine, mind-body practices, energy medicine, acupuncture, homeopathy, chiropractic, Ayurveda), and how such practices are integrated into Western medicine are discussed. Includes lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on learning.
restriction: Non-Biological Science majors only.
overlap: BIO SCI 9J, BIO SCI 9D, BIO SCI 10, BIO SCI D124.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Cell Biology
description: Analysis of the basic structure and function of animal cells, with an emphasis on the regulation of cellular processes. The basic features of membranes, cellular compartmentalization, protein trafficking, vesicular transport, cytoskeleton, adhesion, signal transduction, and cell cycle are covered.

instructors.title: Claire Trevor Professor
instructors.department: Claire Trevor School of the Arts - Studio Art

instructors.title: Professor and Department Graduate Faculty Advisor

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99
restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Developmental Biology
description: Cellular and molecular analysis of how a fertilized egg develops into an organism consisting of complex structures such as the eye, arms, and brain. Emphasis is on the key concepts of developmental processes underlying pattern formation, growth, and regeneration.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99
restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Cell, Developmental, and Molecular Biology of Plants
description: Emphasizes the special features of plant cells and plant development as compared to animals. Two central topics: plants' ability to fuel our planet through photosynthesis, and the interactions of plants with microorganisms in making nitrogen available to other life forms.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97
restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Developmental and Cell Biology Laboratory
description: Covers the division of cells, isolate cellular organelles (chloroplasts, mitochondria, nuclei), and follows changes in cells undergoing programmed cell death. Development is demonstrated in experiments showing cooperation of individual cells in forming a multicellular organism. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and (BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104)
restriction: Seniors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment
corequisites: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Genetics Majors Seminar
description: Genetics majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times
restriction: Genetics majors only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Developmental and Cell Biology Majors Seminar
description: Developmental and Cell Biology majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times
restriction: Developmental and Cell Biology majors only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Human Reproduction and Development PBL Course
description: Focuses on human reproductive biology and in utero human development. Taught in a problem-based learning (PBL) format focused on the biological, social, economic, and ethical implications of specific clinical cases.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 93 and BIO SCI 94 and BIO SCI 97 and BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Movement and Health
description: Mechanisms of movements of molecules within and across cell membranes, cytoskeleton and cell motility, muscle contraction, and physical exercises and mind-body practices. Chemical, electromagnetic, and vital energy, and regulatory pathways in such processes. Relevance to health, diseases, and integrative medicine.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Stem Cell Biology
description: Introduces upper-level undergraduate students to stem cell biology. Include the basic biology of stem cells, potential applications of stem cells, and the ethical, legal, and moral issues associated with human stem cell research.

instructors.name: Leslie F. Lock
instructors.title: UCI Retiree
instructors.department: Sue and Bill Gross Stem Cell Research Center

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103 and BIO SCI D104.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biology of Integrative Medecine
description: Presentation of biological principles and the latest clinical and basic research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., mind-body medicine, energy medicine, herbal medicine, acupuncture, manipulative therapies) and their integration with Western medicine. Lectures supplemented by demonstrations and hands-on learning sessions.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: The Biology and Genetics of Cancer
description: Cancer is a major field in modern biology. Topics discussed include genetics, cellular oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and molecular targets for diagnosis and therapy.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biotechnology and Plant Breeding
description: Conventional plant breeding techniques, their limitations, and supplementations through modern biotechnology. Includes cloning, cell transformation (genetic engineering), and cell fusion. Crop improvement, state of the art in animal and human systems, and the impact of gene technology of society.

instructors.name: Kimberly Krishun Kelley
instructors.title: Project Manager-NURSE-OC
instructors.department: Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Photomedicine
description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.

instructors.name: Michelle Digman
instructors.title: William J. Link Chair and Professor

prerequisiteText: PHYSICS 3C or PHYSICS 7D
restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Precision Medicine
description: Introduction to the use of genomic techniques for the study of individual genomes and transcriptomes in healthy and diseased samples. Covers GWAS, current sequencing techniques, cancer genomics, and biomarker discovery.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advances in Regenerative Medicine
description: Introduces the rapidly growing field of regenerative medicine. New developments in stem cell research are discussed. Cellular, molecular, and engineering aspects of stem cell-based organ replacement strategies are examined, with emphasis on specific regenerative therapies.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Cell Biology of Human Disease
description: Builds on prior biology courses about the underlying cell biological mechanisms and recent treatment advances of several model diseases. Emphasizes literature searches, reading primary literature, and student group work.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Human Anatomy
description: Presents a systems approach to the analysis of human structure. Molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, and organ system levels of structure and organization are integrated throughout.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Eukaryotic and Human Genetics
description: Structure and function of genes in eukaryotes with emphasis on special problems of genetic studies in humans. Molecular methods of genetic analysis and gene transfer are discussed. Practical applications and ethical and social issues raised by genetic studies are addressed.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Critical Thinking in Cell Biology
description: Builds on prior biology courses about cell biology, and works to develop a deeper understanding of experimental techniques and interpretation of experiments. A key focus will be the question of how one moves from specific examples to general.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Intercellular Signaling and Disease
description: Introduces cell-to-cell communication mechanisms, which are fundamentally essential but still not well understood. From well-established to cutting-edge, researches of intercellular communication and how its malfunction leads to diseases are discussed.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: How to Read a Science Paper
description: Provides junior and senior undergraduates currently involved or interested in pursuing research exposure to current scientific literature and training on how to read and critically evaluate primary research articles in preparation for research-oriented.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99
restriction: Upper-division students only.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Genomics, Development, and Medicine
description: Focuses on the applications of genomics and proteomics to problems in genetics, cell, and developmental biology. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the techniques currently used for genomics analysis and how best to apply these tools to solve problems.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Development and Disease
description: Development of animal embryos from a fertilized egg to a functioning organism. Topics include reproduction, body-axis formation, growth and differentiation of embryonic cells, and organogenesis, with an emphasis on congenital birth defects and diseases that disrupt these processes.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Molecular and Cellular Basis of Disease
description: Provides students with examples of how human disease is usually manifested at the cellular level. The roles of specific molecules and organelles are discussed where their roles in the disease process are understood.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Cell Biology
description: An advanced, integrated view of cell biology. Topics include the cell cycle, the cytoskeleton, the extracellular matrix, signal transduction, the cellular basis of development, and the cell biology of cancer.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI 107.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Applied Human Anatomy
description: Systems approach to analyze the form and function of the human body with an emphasis on applying anatomical concepts to evaluate clinical cases. The laboratory uses human models and a simulated cadaver dissection for structure. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 with a minimum grade of C or PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Topics in Developmental and Cell Biology
description: Studies in selected areas of developmental and cell biology.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99
repeatability: May be taken 3 times as topics vary
restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Processes in Ecology and Evolution
description: An in-depth study of the mechanisms that drive evolution and ecology including: natural selection, mutation, genetic drift, speciation, extinction, life history patterns, population dynamics, ecosystem and community structure, predator-prey and host pathogen interactions, and social behavior.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94

dependencies.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World
Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Habitats and Organisms
description: Introduces students to local habitats and organisms through required field trips and applies ecological and evolutionary principles from BIO SCI E106. Students also explore related literature.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. BIO SCI E106L may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after taking BIO SCI E166. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Invited speakers, graduate students, and faculty present current research in ecology and evolutionary biology.
restriction: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Human Physiology
description: Functional features of the major organ systems in the human body. Emphasis on homeostasis and the interactions of organ systems in health and disease. (Discussion of behavior and brain function deferred to BIO SCI N110.)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Physiology Laboratory
description: Laboratory with a focus on the whole organism and its organ systems. Examples of structure-function relationships are drawn from both animal and human physiology. Cellular and molecular aspects are introduced as required. Materials Fee

instructors.title: Professor of Teaching and Vice Chair

restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution Laboratory
description: Students perform experiments which illustrate important concepts in evolutionary biology such as natural selection, random genetic drift, inbreeding, age-specific selection, sexual selection, and phylogenetic reconstruction. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120) and BIO SCI E112L and BIO SCI E183

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E117A
restriction: Exercise Sciences majors only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E117B
restriction: Exercise Sciences majors only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Ecosystem Ecology
description: A mechanistic perspective on ecosystem processes. Covers ecosystem development, element cycling, and interactions with plants and microbes. The role of ecosystems in environmental change is also addressed.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106 or EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 60A or CHEM 51C

prerequisites.title: Fundamental Processes in Earth and Environmental Studies

restriction: Earth System Science majors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and Environmental Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Selfish DNA
description: Focuses on the genetics and evolution of selfish DNA, and introduces necessary background knowledge from molecular biology, cytogenetics, and bioinformatics.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H94 or BIO SCI H97

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Marine Biology
description: Examines the biotic and abiotic factors influencing the physiology, distribution, abundances, interactions, and evolution of marine organisms and the roles of those organisms in mediating ecosystem services and functions. A field trip is required. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Physiology and Pathology of the Kidney
description: Examines the structure, function, and pathology of the kidney. Topics include anatomy of the kidney, cellular function, urine formation, and disease states of the kidney.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Infectious Disease Dynamics
description: Learn how the immune system interacts with infectious diseases, in particular with viral infections. An introduction to basic virology and immunology, it concentrates on the way in which the immune system is critical to the prevention of infections.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Parasitology
description: Parasitism is the most common animal lifestyle. Yet, because parasites are invisible, they are often overlooked. Explore parasite diversity, disease dynamics, and more with an emphasis on the influential roles that parasites play on ecosystem structure and function.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94
restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Physiological Plant Ecology
description: An examination of the interactions between plants and their environment. Emphasis on the underlying physiological mechanisms of plant function, adaptations and responses to stress, and the basis of the distribution of plants and plant assemblages across the landscape.
prerequisiteText: EARTHSS 51 or BIO SCI 94 or EARTHSS 40B
restriction: Biological Sciences majors and Earth System Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Chemical Ecology
description: An introduction to the unspoken chemical language of nature. Emphasis on interactions between insects, plants, and microbes including plant defense, pollination, and microbial warfare.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94) and CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C-

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Forensic Genetics
description: Covers techniques currently used for forensic identification and paternity testing. Topics include STR, Y-STR and mitochondrial DNA tests, database searches, mixtures, allelic drop out, likelihood ratios, laboratory errors and the interaction of science and the legal system.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 93 and BIO SCI 94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Image Analysis in Biological Research
description: Introduction to scientific image analysis including techniques such as high-speed, time-lapse, thermal imaging, and flow visualization. Students make movies using cameras, edit and analyze images using computers, and do a writing project.

instructors.name: Catherine Loudon
instructors.title: Professor of Teaching and Vice Chair

prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI E106 or PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109) and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Diversity of Fishes
description: A survey of the many dimensions of diversity existing across fishes, the largest group of vertebrate organisms (over 30,000 species). Covers systematics, functional anatomy, development, physiology, biogeography, behavior, and more.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Focuses on non-pathogenic microbes within all habitats (soils, oceans, associated with animals and plants) and their essential functions for ecosystems. Their applied importance for agriculture, bioremediation, energy and food production are also discussed.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Microbiomes
description: Students develop an understanding of microbiomes in the context of both their environment and their impact on host physiology. Discussions on how microbiomes interact with the human body.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI M122

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Molecular Evolution
description: Introduction to the study of evolutionary change in genes and DNA sequences. Combines study of molecular biology with the study of evolution. Molecular evolution has application to many disciplines, including molecular biology, virology, systematics, and the origin of life.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: The Physiology of Human Nutrition
description: Examines the biochemical basis of energy metabolism, physiological processes in digestion and uptake, and the biochemical transformation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins in the human body. The emphasis is on expanding the students' understanding of physiology.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98 and (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Genetics of Complex Traits
description: Many ecologically important traits (e.g., size, age at sexual maturity) and clinical conditions are rooted in the interaction of multiple genetic loci with the environment. Theoretical and practical approaches to dissecting the genetic architecture of complex traits are explored.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: Maintenance aspects of physiology: water balance; feeding and digestion; metabolism; respiration and circulation.

instructors.name: Catherine Loudon
instructors.title: Professor of Teaching and Vice Chair

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Animal Locomotion
description: The physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience that determines how animals propel themselves and navigate through the world. Considers the principles that govern the walking, running, flying, and swimming of animals, including exercising humans.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution and the Environment
description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves discussion of scientific journal articles and other readings, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
prerequisiteText: Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI E106.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution and the Environment Laboratory
description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves lab activities and discussion of scientific journal articles, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Writing/Philosophy of Biology
description: Philosophy of biology, e.g., scientific method in biology, the structure of evolutionary theory, teleology, ethics, and evolution. Course work includes one 4,000-word and four 1,000-word papers.
prerequisiteText: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
restriction: Juniors only.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Animal Coloration and Vision
description: Physiological and behavioral mechanisms of color production and vision including crypsis, mimicry, aposematism, masquerade, sexual dimorphism, and predator-prey interactions through the lens of signals, receivers, and receptors; color and polarization vision in mate choice and visual adaptations to aquatic environments.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106 (may be taken concurrently)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Ecosystem Services
description: Covers what ecosystem services are, how to classify them, what the impacts of land degradation are on ecosystem services, how to quantify and value them, and the importance of mainstreaming ecosystem services in decision-making.
prerequisiteText: (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B) or (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53 and EARTHSS 55)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Behavioral Endocrinology
description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Conservation Biology
description: Genetic and ecological issues in conservation biology, including effects of human population growth, the value of biodiversity, conservation genetics, demography, metapopulation dynamics, community and ecosystem processes, species invasions, global climate change, and reserve design and management.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
description: Interactions between organisms and their environments. Topics include the effects of environmental variables on biochemical functions: membrane stability, protein kinetics, energy metabolism, heat-shock-responses, energetics, gene-expression, and circadian rhythms. These topics are integrated with physiological-ecology in context of global climate change.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Genetics and Human History
description: Explores topics in human health/history from an evolutionary perspective, with emphasis on genetics. Topics include the relationship between genetics and human disease as an evolutionary question, and how modern genetic techniques are used to study the history of human populations.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106 (may be taken concurrently)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Physiology in Extreme Environments
description: An in-depth look at the physiological mechanisms that allow animals, including humans, to be physically active and survive in extreme environments. Physiological responses to high altitude, diving, microgravity, deserts, and extreme cold are examined.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
description: Structure and evolution of the major organ systems in vertebrates, from fish to mammals.  Materials fee.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biology of Birds
description: A thorough introduction to the biology of birds, covering topics ranging from avian anatomy and physiology to behavior, natural history, ecology, genetics, evolution, systematics, and conservation. Examples from both local and global avifauna.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biology of Birds Lab
description: The companion to Biology of Birds (E160). Consists primarily of field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history. Students must provide their own transportation to field sites, some with entrance fees. Students must have field binoculars.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)
restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biology of Birds Lab
description: The companion to Biology of Birds (E160). Consists primarily of field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history. Students must provide their own transportation to field sites, some with entrance fees. Students must have field binoculars.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI 194S
restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Establishes a fundamental understanding of microbes living in the environment, including their distribution, diversity, and biochemistry, and discusses how they attribute to global biogeochemical cycles.
prerequisiteText: (EARTHSS 53) or (EARTHSS 60A and EARTHSS 60C) or (BIO SCI E106 and BIO SCI M122)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Field Biology
description: Conducting group and independent studies in Southern California ecosystems, this course covers the fundamentals of experimental design, statistical analysis, communicating scientific findings (orally, visually, in writing), and other skills necessary for the scientific investigation of biological processes in the field. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement
restriction: Seniors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Field Methods in Ecology
description: Field studies of major concepts in plant and animal ecology, with emphasis on experimental design, field sampling methods, statistical analysis, and scientific writing. An independent project and two field trips are required.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI E106. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution
description: An integrative treatment of evolutionary biology that covers evolutionary processes, basic research methods, and the history of life.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Mechanical Physiology
description: Explores the mechanics of animal physiology. Basic biomechanical principles are introduced and illustrated in a variety of physiological systems. Topics include the fluid and structural mechanics of muscles, skeletons, circulation, insect flight, biomaterials, and fish swimming.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World
description: Investigation of planet diversity in California and throughout the world, including basic systematic concepts, an introduction to major groups of flowering plants, and the effects of global biological change on plant diversity.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Plant Systematics Laboratory
description: Diversity of flowering plants is investigated in the laboratory and field. Familiarity with flowering plant families, particularly those prominent in the California flora, is emphasized.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106 and BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI 194S. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI E172.

prerequisites.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World

restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Behavioral Ecology
description: Animal behavior as an evolutionary solution to problems encountered during an animal's life cycle. Includes a broad comparative approach to communication, social behavior, habitat selection, and food finding.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Restoration Ecology
description: Theoretical and practical aspects of habitat restoration and mitigation. Design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects in local habitats. Collection of seed and cuttings, planting and maintenance presented. Control of exotics in natural areas discussed. Environmental ethics of restoration emphasized.   Materials fee.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Evolution of Infectious Disease
description: Introduction to the major human pathogens, and the ecological and evolutionary processes affecting their impact on public health. Topics include the evolution of drug resistance, problems in vaccine development, diseases emerging from animals, and bioterrorism.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Ocean Ecology
description: Examines the relationships between physical processes in the ocean, biological productivity, and the exploitation of ocean resources by high-trophic-level predators, including humans. Discusses open ocean ecosystems, intertidal and benthic regions of the world ocean.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Limnology and Freshwater Biology
description: Biology of freshwater environments: lakes, ponds, rivers, their biota, and the factors which influence distribution of organisms.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Field Freshwater Ecology
description: Analytical techniques for common water-quality variables of lakes, streams, and rivers. Benthic fauna, vertebrates and invertebrates, algae, and aquatic plants. Emphasis on field methods with an experimental approach; laboratory exercises. Field trips to marshes, vernal pools, rivers, and streams. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E179
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Conservation in the American West
description: Critical examination of contemporary conservation issues in the American West, with particular attention to water in California, grazing on public lands, and species decline and extinctions.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Mediterranean Ecosystems: Biodiversity and Conservation
description: Biodiversity, history of human impacts, and conservation efforts are examined in the five Mediterranean-type ecosystems. Remaining natural habitat, approaches to ecological habitat restoration, control of exotic species, and predicted consequences of global climate change are described. Field trip required.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 94

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Exercise Physiology
description: Focus upon critical topics in the area of exercise biology using the comparative physiological approach. Specifically examine the physiological factors that limit the capacity of an organism to sustain high levels of aerobic metabolism.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Ecology and Diversity of Insects
description: Insects—representing two-thirds of all species—play fundamental roles in human health, agriculture, and natural ecosystems. Topics include insect morphology, development, physiology, taxonomy, ecology, and insects in human affairs. Lecture includes interactive demonstrations and an optional weekend trip. Materials Fee
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Population and Community Ecology
description: Population structure, function, development, and evolution. Topics include population structure, population growth and regulation, metapopulations, predation, competition, species diversity, ecosystem function, macroecology, and island biogeography. Offered every other Winter.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Population and Community Ecology Lab
description: Covers processes specific to groups of the same species (populations) and multiple species (communities). Includes growth, regulation, dynamics, and persistence of populations and community interactions, development, diversity, and macroecology. Lab activities focus on application of population prediction and biodiversity assessment.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Exercise as Medicine
description: Explores the link between regular physical activity and health, focusing on mechanistic insights into how regular exercise improves overall health and alters disease trajectories of cancer, type-II diabetes, depression, and other chronic illnesses.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Insect Physiology
description: Physiology of insects. Insect respiration, digestion, excretion, and neurobiology, including sensory systems and effectors.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Environmental Ethics
description: History of evolution of environmental ethics in America. Management problems in national parks, wilderness areas, wild and scenic rivers, national forests. Contemporary and historical aspects/contributors to the field. Mitigation, endangered species, habitat restoration, biodiversity, and environmental activism. Field trips required.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Studies in selected areas of ecology and evolutionary biology.

instructors.name: Catherine Loudon
instructors.title: Professor of Teaching and Vice Chair

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI E106
repeatability: May be taken 3 times as topics vary

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors Topics in Biological Sciences
description: Varied course topics in Biological Sciences designed for students in Honors in Biological Sciences.
repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times
restriction: School of Biological Sciences Honors students only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors Writing for Biological Research
description: Science writing and critical reasoning. Work, research, and writing exercises are conducted in a computer laboratory. Preliminary writing exercises and further development of Excellence in Research to a full scientific senior thesis. This forms the basis for an oral defense.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 199. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
restriction: Excellence in Research Program students only.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors Physiology
description: Contemporary research problems in physiology using insects as model systems. Topics include digestion, osmoregulation, development, and neurobiology, including sensory systems and behavior. Participating students present papers in a journal club-style format and write short essays summarizing research findings.
restriction: Biological Sciences Honors Program students only. Graduate students only.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors Virus Evolution
description: Viruses infect all domains of life and have had profound consequences on the development and survival of life. Examines virus emergence and evolution in a broad context. Weekly overview is followed by student presentations and essays based on contemporary literature.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI M124A.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
description: The importance of biological sciences in our world is discussed. Topics may include brain and behavior, health and disease, genetics and society, and conservation biology. Primary goal is to encourage students to understand better the world in which they live.

instructors.name: Rudi C Berkelhamer
instructors.title: Senior Lecturer SOE - Emeritus, Assoc.Dean- UCI Retiree

restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors From DNA to Organisms
description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology or organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).
restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors From Organisms to Ecosystems
description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.

instructors.name: Catherine Loudon
instructors.title: Professor of Teaching and Vice Chair

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI H93
restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Honors Genetics
description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.

dependencies.title: Cell, Developmental, and Molecular Biology of Plants

restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only. BIO SCI H97 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 97

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Biochemistry
description: Physical-chemical properties of macromolecules. Structure-function relationships in nucleic acids, protein, carbohydrates, and lipids. Integration and regulation of metabolism. Biochemistry of organs and biochemistry of diseases.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biochemistry Laboratory
description: Properties of enzymes and the culture and isolation of mutants of microorganisms. Materials Fee

instructors.title: Staff Research Associate
instructors.department: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Allied Health Microbiology
description: Introductory microbiology lecture and laboratory with an emphasis on microbial growth control and the relationship between microbes and human health.
prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93) and CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C-
restriction: School of Nursing students have the first consideration for enrollment
overlap: BIO SCI M122, BIO SCI M118L

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Molecular Biology
description: Mechanisms of gene expression; special emphasis on regulatory events that occur in Eukaryotic organisms other than initiation of transcription. Chromatin structure and rearrangement, RNA polymerases, cis- and trans-acting elements, RNA processing, transport and stability, protein synthesis, trafficking, and turnover.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
description: Students perform experiments which illustrate the chemical and biological properties of nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on recent techniques in recombinant DNA technology including gene isolation and characterization. Materials Fee

instructors.title: UCI Retiree
instructors.department: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Experimental Microbiology Laboratory
description: Introductory general microbiology designed for preprofessional biology majors. Includes microscopy, cultivation of bacteria, morphological and biochemical characterization of bacteria, microbial metabolism, growth and genetics, microorganisms and human disease, and interactions of microorganisms with the environment. Materials Fee

instructors.title: Academic Coordinator
instructors.department: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.

instructors.name: Paolo Casali
instructors.title: Donald Bren Prof Medicine, Molecular Biology & Biochemistry

restriction: Microbiology and Immunology majors have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Signal Transduction in Mammalian Cells
description: Introduction to major biochemical pathways that transmit information from extracellular cues into changes in cell behavior. Focuses on kinases, phosphateses, G proteins, second messengers, and protein-protein interactions. Includes discussion of primary research articles and experimental techniques.

instructors.name: Craig Walsh
instructors.title: Professor, Associate Dean of Graduate Education

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI D103

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Immunology with Hematology
description: Antibodies, antigens, antigen-antibody reactions, cells and tissues of lymphoreticular and hematopoietic systems, and individual and collective components of cell-mediated and humoral immune response.

instructors.name: Christopher C Hughes
instructors.title: Professor and Assoc Dean for Research & Innovation

instructors.name: Craig Walsh
instructors.title: Professor, Associate Dean of Graduate Education

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
description: Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, and immunofluorescent staining assays. Materials Fee

instructors.title: Professor and Assoc Dean for Research & Innovation

instructors.title: Professor, Associate Dean of Graduate Education

prerequisiteText: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI M121
restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: General Microbiology
description: Comparative metabolism of small molecules and cell structure and relationship to microbial classification. Macromolecule synthesis and regulation, sporulation, cell division, growth, and effect of antibiotics.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Microbiology Laboratory
description: Advanced course featuring selective isolation of a wide variety of microbial types. Identification and characterization of organisms by morphological, nutritional, and biochemical approaches. Medical, industrial, and research applications.  Materials fee.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 194S. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100 and (BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M132).
restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introduction to Computational Biology
description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
prerequisiteText: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Virology
description: Replication of viruses in populations, animals, and the host cell. The effects of viral infection on populations, individuals, and specific molecular effects on the target cell. Role of viral infections in cancer and degenerative diseases.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99
restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Viral Pathogenesis and Immunity
description: The mechanisms of viral pathogenesis and of host resistance to viruses are explored in detail. HIV-1 and Influenza-A are used as examples. In each case, viral replication, cytopathic effects, immune response, and viral evasion are discussed.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A. Recommended: BIO SCI M122

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Virus Engineering Laboratory
description: An advanced laboratory for undergraduates who have completed a virology lecture class. Students learn to engineer recombinant viruses and express genes in mouse tissue.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI M116L and (BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B). Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100.
restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Molecular Biology of Cancer
description: Molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis. Consideration of transformation by DNA tumor viruses, RNA tumor viruses, and chemical carcinogens.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Learning to Read Primary Literature in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: An introduction to primary literature focusing on methods to approach, understand, and analyze scientific papers.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Virology and Immunology Laboratory
description: Introductory laboratory course in virology and immunology designed for biology majors. Curriculum includes plasmid preparation, plasmid characterization, microscopy, cell culture, transfection and infection of cells, cell counting, plaque assays, ELISA, Western blot, mixed lymphocyte reactions.  Materials fee.

instructors.name: Craig Walsh
instructors.title: Professor, Associate Dean of Graduate Education

prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99 and BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI M116L
restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
corequisites: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Introductory Bioinformatics Lab
description: An introduction to modern methods of analyzing genomic, transcriptomic, and protein structure data. Students design experiments, extract information from a variety of different public databases and synthesize information to gain a deeper understanding of biological systems.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)
restriction: Seniors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Discovery of the New RNA World
description: Focus is on RNAs role in catalysis and regulation. Topics include non-coding RNAs function in normal cells (regulation of cell homeostasis, development, and differentiation) and in disease (cancer, viral infection).
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104).

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Advanced Molecular Lab Techniques
description: Discovery-driven experimentation in the fields of molecular biology, biochemistry, and cell biology. Also involves other aspects of the lab experience including group discussion of results, scientific paper analysis, and student presentations.   Materials fee.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 100 and (BIO SCI D111L or BIO SCI M114L or BIO SCI M116L or BIO SCI M118L)
repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.
restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Innate Immunity, Infection, and Pathogenesis
description: Role of the innate immune system in health and disease. Molecular pathways of innate immune recognition, expression, and regulation of immune receptors, signal transduction, pathogen sensors, and detection of microbial ligands. Lecture and discussion of primary research articles.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B or BIO SCI M143

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Structural Biology
description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, X-ray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
prerequisiteText: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4
restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Microbial Genetics
description: Basic principles of microbial genetics are presented as lectures for the first half of the course. The second half is devoted to applications of these principles and requires reading review and original research papers and interactions with guest lecturers.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Human Parasitology
description: Introduction to human animal-parasitic diseases including worms and protozoan infections.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Cell Organelles and Membranes
description: Structure, function, and biogenesis of biological membranes and membrane-bound organelles.
prerequisiteText: CHEM 51A

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Nutritional Biochemistry
description: Metabolic processes of sugar and fat that lead to an understanding of diabetes, cancer, obesity and other disease states will be the focus of this course.  Nutritional supplements, analysis of metabolites and mechanisms of metabolic enzymes will be covered.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Vascular Biology: Blood Vessels in Health and Disease
description: Every cell in the body is within a half hair’s width of a blood vessel. As such, we cannot understand the body, in health or disease, without understanding the vasculature. Mixes lectures and primary literature reviews.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 99

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Structure-Function Relationships of Integral Membrane Proteins
description: Integral membrane proteins such as voltage and ligand-gated ion channels, water channels, pumps, cotransporters, and receptors (e.g., GPCRs). The emphasis is on the relationship between atomic structure and the functional properties of these proteins.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99. BIO SCI 98 with a grade of B or better. BIO SCI 99 with a grade of B or better

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Biotechnological Applications of Energy and Environmental Research
description: Covers microbiological and biochemical background related to current biotechnological applications, case studies of biotech-companies, and basic information related to patents and start-up companies. Topics include biofuel, bioremediation, agricultural, and environmental applications.
prerequisiteText: BIO SCI 98

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Topics in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
description: Studies in selected areas of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.

school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
title: Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Consideration of the evolution of behavior, including ethological and psychological aspects and analysis of neuroanatomical, neurochemical, neurophysiological, and neuroendocrine systems underlying basic behavioral processes.
